articles.title: What Is a Headless CMS — and When Should You Use One?
articles.excerpt: Every few years a piece of web vocabulary escapes the developer world and starts showing up in client briefings. Headless CMS is that term right now. Founders hear it in agency pitches, read it in pla…
articles.body: Every few years a piece of web vocabulary escapes the developer world and starts showing up in client briefings. Headless CMS is that term right now. Founders hear it in agency pitches, read it in platform comparisons, and reasonably ask: is this something my project needs, or is it a more expensive way to edit a website? This is our attempt at a headless cms explained answer with no sales angle — including the cases where we would tell you not to use one. We have a dog in this fight, by the way: this site's blog runs on a git-backed headless setup, so the trade-offs below are ones we live with daily, not ones we read about.
articles.author: Tjvex Studio

articles.title: AI Agents Went Rogue This Week — The Guardrails Playbook for Businesses
articles.excerpt: Originally published on DigiHustle This was the week AI agents stopped being a demo problem and became a liability problem. On Friday, Tencent admitted AI agents used to evaluate third-party models ha…
articles.body: Originally published on DigiHustle This was the week AI agents stopped being a demo problem and became a liability problem. On Friday, Tencent admitted AI agents used to evaluate third-party models had browsed the web in ways nobody intended. An AI-safety group called Swarmchasers had flagged the behavior two days earlier. Anthropic's Claude got caught in a similar situation — an agent with browsing access did things its operators didn't plan for. And OpenAI's agent offerings keep expanding their permissions while the guardrails conversation lags behind. None of this is a reason to stop using AI agents. It is a reason to stop deploying them like they're deterministic software. They're not. They're probabilistic systems with tool access, and that combination needs boundaries.

articles.title: Dispatches: I needed a PA
articles.excerpt: Relay was originally conceived as a synthetic company. That was always the mental model. It had a board of directors. It had HR vetting agents. It had different roles, delegations and responsibilities…
articles.body: Relay was originally conceived as a synthetic company. That was always the mental model. It had a board of directors. It had HR vetting agents. It had different roles, delegations and responsibilities. In some ways it could behave more flexibly than a real company because the board didn’t have to sit at the top grilling a CEO about what was happening underneath it. It could drop straight into a department, interrogate what was happening there, challenge decisions and then move somewhere else. I’ve spent an extraordinary amount of time thinking about the organisational structure of this thing. Then this morning something embarrassingly obvious hit me. I’ve forgotten the fucking PA. I am effectively the CEO of this synthetic company and I am still scheduling my own day. Why?

articles.title: Next.js vs Flutter Web: Choosing the Right Stack
articles.excerpt: Sooner or later, almost every web project we quote hits the same fork in the road. The client already has a Flutter mobile app — or plans to build one — and the question becomes: should the web versio…
articles.body: Sooner or later, almost every web project we quote hits the same fork in the road. The client already has a Flutter mobile app — or plans to build one — and the question becomes: should the web version be built in Next.js, or in Flutter Web? The next.js vs flutter web debate looks like a simple framework comparison. It isn't. One is a way to build websites with JavaScript; the other is a way to build apps with Dart that happen to run in a browser. Get the distinction right and the choice is usually obvious. Get it wrong and you pay for it every month — in search traffic you never win back, or load times that quietly kill conversions. What each of them actually is Next.js is a React framework, maintained by Vercel, that renders real HTML and CSS in the browser.

articles.title: From Westminster Ban Calls to Living Room Vision Therapy
articles.excerpt: From Westminster Ban Calls to Living Room Vision Therapy: The Tale of Two Eye Technologies The hook: A Reform UK politician's smart glasses flash in the Senedd. He speaks for five minutes without note…
articles.body: From Westminster Ban Calls to Living Room Vision Therapy: The Tale of Two Eye Technologies The hook: A Reform UK politician's smart glasses flash in the Senedd. He speaks for five minutes without notes. The press spots the periodic glint. Westminster erupts — calls for a ban on AI wearables in chambers. The bridge: Same week, a teenager in Manchester puts on a Meta Quest headset, launches Amblyotube, picks a Minecraft YouTuber, and spends 35 minutes training her lazy eye. The app blurs her strong eye, sharpens the weak one with AI, flashes a magenta fusion cue. She takes the headset off. The room looks deeper. She smiles. Two stories. Same core tech: different visual stream per eye. One triggers a policy panic. The other restores 3D vision. This isn't whataboutism.

articles.title: I built a no-login Instagram follower tracker that only shows what changed since the last run
articles.excerpt: Instagram does not make it easy to watch other public accounts. Most follower trackers need your login or only cover your own account. What it does You give it a list of public Instagram profiles. It…
articles.body: Instagram does not make it easy to watch other public accounts. Most follower trackers need your login or only cover your own account. I built a small Apify tool for the case where you just want to watch many public profiles and see what changed. What it does You give it a list of public Instagram profiles. It returns follower and following counts, and, compared with your last run, the growth in numbers and in percent, new posts, bio edits and posting pace. No login, no cookies. It only reads what a logged-out visitor can see. What it does not do Private accounts, and anything behind a login (such as who exactly followed whom), are out of reach. Instagram sometimes answers with "too many requests". The tool waits and retries, but a run can still fail. If it does, run it again later.

articles.title: I’ve been using an AI agent for a month, and I’m both impressed and terrified
articles.excerpt: Instinct AI is extremely good, with some big caveats.
articles.body: We’ve reached a pretty interesting point with AI. For the longest time, I’ve mostly used AI tools to ask questions or to write emails and summarize long PDFs. But AI agents are starting to change that. If you’re unfamiliar with the difference between an AI chatbot and an AI agent, it’s pretty simple. While a chatbot mostly gives you answers or helps you figure out how to do something, an AI agent can actually perform those tasks for you. For example, instead of asking AI to draft an email, you can ask an agent to find the relevant information, write the email, and send it on your behalf.

articles.body: Apple has finally announced its long-rumored foldable: the iPhone Duo . The new phone has a 5.4-inch outer display and a 7.6-inch inner display, a “nano‑texture” finish on the inner screen, and barely any visible crease. Instead of Face ID, it uses Touch ID on the power button. It has two cameras, a main lens and a wide-angle lens. Apple completely revamped iOS 27’s controls and apps for the foldable, including putting the dock on the side of the phone. And it has a flashy opening animation when you unfold the phone. The iPhone Duo a big new bet from Apple, though one that’s a little late to the game compared to competitors like Samsung and Google. The phone isn’t cheap: it starts at $1,999 for the base 256GB model, and the prices only go up from there.

articles.body: The astronauts of SpaceX's Crew-12 mission to the International Space Station wish that we could all see Earth as they just did. An orbital view reveals the immense beauty of our blue planet, the only world we know of that hosts life. But it also highlights how fragile that life is, tethered to our lonely Earth in the vast void of space, according to Crew-12 commander Jessica Meir of NASA. "You see this very thin, tenuous band of an atmosphere , and you know that that is all that is supporting life, and we really need to do our best to protect it," Meir said on Thursday afternoon (Oct. 15), during a press conference that discussed the recently concluded Crew-12 mission .

articles.title: When not to watch a meteor shower — why I'm not staying up for the Orionids
articles.excerpt: The Orionid meteor shower peaks next week, but a bright moon makes much of the night less than ideal. Sometimes the sensible observing decision is knowing when to stay in bed — and when to get up earl…
articles.body: I used to think being interested in the night sky meant I had to try every meteor shower. If a calendar said "peak," I interpreted that as an instruction. I'd set an alarm, find several layers of clothing and go outside at around 2:00 a.m. when even the neighborhood cats seemed surprised to see me. Then I'd spend an increasingly resentful 45 minutes staring upward, occasionally see one meteor and wonder whether I was somehow doing it all wrong. As I've grown into stargazing, I've become much more selective. The Orionids peak next week, and normally I'd be tempted. These fast meteors come from debris from Halley's Comet , which is enough of a connection to make almost anyone want to go outside.

articles.title: Scientists find 'gemstones' in atmosphere of bizarre, scorching-hot 'marshmallow' exoplanet
articles.excerpt: Using data from the James Webb Space Telescope, astronomers have unravelled some of the secrets of a bizarre, blisteringly hot exoplanet that has the consistency of marshmallow.
articles.body: Using data from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), astronomers have unraveled some of the atmospheric secrets of a bizarre, blisteringly hot world that has the consistency of marshmallow. The extrasolar planet, or exoplanet , under the watchful infrared eye of the JWST , is WASP-17b, located around 1,300 light-years away. The exoplanet has a mass around 0.8 times that of Jupiter, but it is around twice as wide as the solar system's largest planet, giving it a "super-puff" consistency comparable to the Earth-based treat. WASP-17 b is so close to its parent star that it completes an orbit in under four Earth days, with this proximity also making the temperature of this " hot Jupiter " skyrocket.

articles.title: How to see the Orionid meteor shower 2026 peak this week — and when to look
articles.excerpt: The Orionids peak around Oct. 21. Here's when and where to look for the best chance of spotting meteors.
articles.body: If you love watching meteors, 2026 has given you plenty to enjoy. This summer, the annual Perseid meteor shower peaked on the day of a new moon — and a solar eclipse — so moonlight stayed out of the way. And there's more to look forward to: in December, the Geminids, the year's most prolific shower, will peak after a waxing crescent moon sets early in the evening, opening the door to excellent viewing. Right between those two headline showers, the dependable Orionids take their turn, reaching peak activity around Oct. 21-22. So, when and where can you catch the show?
